instructions: Heat 4 cups of water in a kettle or small pot until hot.
Meanwhile, put the rice and lentils in a fine sieve and rinse them under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Drain well. Finely chop the onion.
Heat the oil in a 3-quart pot with a lid over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, until soft.
Add the rice and lentils and stir for 2 minutes, until the rice looks a little see-through and smells toasty.
Pour in the hot water and add the salt and pepper. Stir once and bring it to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 18 minutes. No peeking.
Take the pot off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. The lentils will have softened into the rice.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: All three sources cook the rice and lentils together as a pilaf with fat and a long covered rest; Lezzet (the lead, no rating shown) does it in one pot with rice and lentils at 1 to 1, while Almost Turkish uses green lentils boiled first and an onion softened in the fat. This version follows Lezzet's one-pot method and Almost Turkish's onion, and uses red lentils because they cook in the same time as the rice. The water is 2 cups for each cup of rice and lentils together, and the rest is 5 minutes, not the 10 to 20 the sources give. It runs about a minute over 35 minutes.
